# Bound autogenerated subtitle downloads

## Summary

Auto-generated subtitle downloads currently combine with `--sub-langs all`, causing yt-dlp to request many YouTube timedtext tracks and fail with rate limits such as HTTP 429.

## Requirements

- Keep auto-generated subtitles enabled.
- Bound the requested subtitle languages to English and the original-language auto-caption track.
- Keep downloaded subtitles converted to WebVTT for existing caption serving.
- Avoid adding a broad configuration surface unless required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- yt-dlp download commands no longer request all subtitle languages by default.
- yt-dlp download commands request English and original-language subtitle tracks.
- yt-dlp download commands still request auto-generated subtitles.
- Tests cover the bounded subtitle language arguments.
- Relevant Go tests pass.

## Notes

- The observed failure attempted to download language `ab`, which indicates a global auto-caption language sweep.
- Superseded by [Tighten yt-dlp subtitle language selection](tighten-ytdlp-subtitle-language-selection.md): the main media command now downloads manual subtitles with `--write-subs --sub-langs all`, and original auto-captions are fetched with a separate `--write-auto-subs --sub-langs .*-orig` command.
